subject: Pilot billing mechanics: escrow and split-entity payment waterfall (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: peter.gray@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot billing question — multi-entity split + VAT handling

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited to move the pilot forward. Before we sign the SOW we need to confirm how Redwood will handle multi-entity invoicing and VAT for the pilot. High-level asks from finance: 

- We need the ability to split a single customer charge across two legal entities (Nimbus US and Nimbus EU) so our accounting can apportion revenue.
- Preferably we want per-line entity tagging on the invoice so each line shows which legal entity issued the tax invoice.
- For EMEA usage there will be VAT that Nimbus needs to reclaim/credit. We need Redwood to: 1) indicate VAT on the EU invoice lines and 2) provide the supporting tax evidence (invoice copy, tax point date) in CSV or PDF.
- For payment routing, we want to evaluate an escrow arrangement (third-party escrow) to ensure funds flow to the right entities after verification — especially for pilot where legal ops wants a single pay event but split disbursement.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) issue per-line entity invoices or sibling invoices; 2) integrate with an escrow provider for a waterfall disbursement; and 3) provide the VAT documentation we need? Also include any expected timeline or required documents on our side.

If easier, happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Finance — Nimbus Health
elena@nimbushealth.com

Attachments: Nimbus_Payment_Requirements_2027.xlsx (see referenced tab: VAT-reclaim)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Short answers up-front: yes, we have two workable patterns (per-line entity tagging or sibling invoices), and we can route payments through an escrow partner with a simple waterfall; we can also export the invoice metadata needed for VAT reclaim. Details and action items below.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben: please outline the two invoice options and note required metadata / file formats we can provide.
- Marissa: please flag any contract/escrow language we should add to the SOW and if there are any regulatory concerns for EU VAT.
- Elena/Peter: if escrow is acceptable we’ll draft an escrow term sheet and share a DocuSign-ready SOW with the billing/payment flow diagram.

Goal: get agreement on the pattern by EOD Wednesday so we can sign and start the pilot the week after.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Peter Gray <peter.gray@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — multi-entity split + VAT handling

Elena / team — working through this from a finance perspective. Summary of recommended approach (tradeoffs included):

Option A — Single consolidated invoice with line-level entity tags (preferred for Nimbus UX):
- Redwood issues one invoice PDF for the customer but each invoice line includes a machine-readable entity tag (GL/Entity ID) and remit-to instructions per line.
- Payment can be made to an escrow account; escrow then disburses to each Redwood legal entity on the configured waterfall.
- Pros: single pay event for Nimbus, single statement of account; easier for ops.
- Cons: requires escrow provider integration and a short settlement lag while escrow validates invoice metadata.

Option B — Sibling invoices (two sibling tax invoices delivered same day):
- Redwood issues two separate tax invoices: one from Redwood US (USD, no VAT) and one from Redwood EU (EUR, VAT applied as needed).
- Nimbus initiates two payment legs or one payment to escrow that disburses to both.
- Pros: straightforward VAT separation; accounting teams get immediate entity-level invoices.
- Cons: slightly more complex for reconciliation if Nimbus prefers a single payment.

VAT and evidence: for Option A we will export a CSV with per-line VAT amounts, tax point dates, and invoice numbers. For EU VAT reclaim Nimbus will need the EU invoice copy and tax point evidence; Redwood can provide consolidated supporting docs via a secure share (PDF + CSV).

Escrow/disbursement: we normally work with ClearLedger Escrow for early-stage pilots. Typical waterfall: 1) escrow receives funds; 2) 48h verification window for invoice metadata; 3) escrow disburses per configured splits; 4) fees (escrow + FX) can be passed through to payer or absorbed per negotiated terms.

Required docs from Nimbus:
- Legal entity names, tax/VAT IDs for each entity
- Remit-to banking details for each Redwood entity (we provide)
- Billing contact and collections contact (for notification flows)

I attached a sample invoice CSV showing the line-level tags and a short sketch of the escrow waterfall. If we proceed I can draft the escrow term sheet and the language to add to the SOW.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_invoice_template.csv, escrow_waterfall_sketch.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing question — multi-entity split + VAT handling

Thanks Ben — quick legal/procurement notes: 

- Escrow addition: we’ll add a short escrow schedule to the SOW that references a standalone escrow agreement (hosted by ClearLedger). SOW will state: "Customer will make a single payment to the Escrow Agent; Redwood and Customer agree to the Escrow Agent's disbursement instructions as set forth in the Escrow Agreement."
- Payment fees: recommend we propose that escrow fees and FX remain the payer's responsibility by default; if Nimbus prefers Redwood to absorb fees for the pilot we can add a line item credit in the SOW.
- Tax representation: Redwood will represent tax charges on EU-issued invoices but cannot provide tax advisory; Nimbus should confirm local reclaim eligibility before relying solely on our documentation.
- Data retention: include a clause ensuring we retain billing metadata for 7 years for audit support (or as otherwise required by local law).

I’ll prepare redlines to the SOW and a short escrow term sheet for Nimbus legal to review. Is Nimbus comfortable with ClearLedger? If not we can accept another escrow provider that meets standard KYC requirements.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to send redlined SOW + escrow term sheet by EOD Tuesday.
2) Nimbus to confirm entity tax IDs and whether they want fees passed through.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_escrow_terms.pdf
